Spelling, Not Switching: Phonetic Normalization for Romanized Hinglish Code-Switched Retrieval

📌 TEACHER'S GOOGLE FORM SUBMISSION FILE
This self-contained document contains full experiment results, data links, analysis tables, and outcome screenshots. All images are embedded inside this file.

1. Project Overview

  • Research Topic: Empirical investigation into retrieval degradation in romanized Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-switched queries across standard BEIR benchmarks.
  • Core Research Question: Does query performance drop primarily because of cross-lingual semantic switching, or non-standard phonetic spelling noise?
  • Proposed Framework: PhonoNorm — training-free 3-tier phonetic normalization evaluated against transliteration, vocabulary expansion, BM25, and dense neural baselines.

5. Key Findings Summary

  1. Switching Cost Dominates Monolingual Encoders: Semantic switching causes 3x–10x greater degradation than spelling noise for BM25, MiniLM, and E5-small.
  2. Multilingual Encoders Uniquely Sensitive to Spelling Noise: BGE-M3 retains cross-lingual semantic stability but significantly degrades under spelling inconsistency (p < 0.003).
  3. PhonoNorm Recovers Human Degradation: On 120 human queries, PhonoNorm brings MiniLM to 0.4836 nDCG@10 (surpassing native English 0.4793) and recovers 25.7% of BM25 drop.
  4. Training-Free Superiority: Lexicon-based phonetic hashing outperforms costly vocabulary expansion without needing any GPU fine-tuning.

6. Experimental Pipeline Reproduction

python scripts/01_download.py         # Download BEIR corpora
python scripts/02_build_lexicon.py     # Build 3-tier phonetic hash dictionary
python scripts/03_generate_queries.py  # Synthesize Hinglish queries
python scripts/05_run_grid.py          # Execute full evaluation grid (466 rows)
python scripts/08_human_eval.py        # Run 120 human CS query evaluations
python scripts/run_significance_v2.py  # 100k permutation Fisher tests
python scripts/06_analysis.py          # Generate publication LaTeX tables
python scripts/07_figures.py           # Render publication figures
